reason: The cited evidence (E1) reports fine grain size (1–35 μm) in a DED-deposited Ti-Nb-Cr-V-Ni-Al alloy, but it does not mention cooling rates, annealing, or mechanical properties. It therefore provides no support for the specific claims about achieving ≥10^4 K/s cooling, the effect of a 950 °C anneal, or the predicted yield strength increase. The alloy composition also differs substantially from the proposed Ti–Ni primary HEA.
premises: Rapid cooling (≥10^4 K/s) during DED can be achieved and will refine grain size in a Ti–Ni primary HEA
A short anneal just below recrystallization temperature (~950 °C) will not cause significant grain growth
Grain refinement in this alloy will increase elevated-temperature yield strength via Hall–Petch strengthening
The cited Ti-Nb-Cr-V-Ni-Al alloy is representative of a Ti–Ni primary HEA
